# Deterministic calendar compatibility suite

Run the contracts with:

```sh
cargo test --locked calendar_compatibility
cargo test --locked custom_timezone::tests
cargo test --locked timezones::tests
```

The `.ics` files are synthetic and contain no personal calendar data. Assertions
live in `src/calendar_compatibility_tests.rs`. They exercise calendar parsing,
timezone lookup/construction, recurrence expansion, exclusions and overrides
through `extract_events_for_year`, with a fixed evaluation year of **2024**.
Production still uses the current local year, captured once at entry.
Event expansion retains the existing 2023–2025 window; timezone construction
uses 2022–2025, retaining the latest earlier onset from each observance.

Expected UTC instants are handwritten, not snapshots generated by the fork.
Every event fixture checks count, ordered starts, ends, display timezone,
all-day status and summary. The New York/Berlin fixture also asserts displayed
wall times while the two regions change DST on different dates.

## Contracts covered

- Weekly local meetings across spring and autumn DST changes.
- Inclusive UTC UNTIL for a local recurrence crossing DST.
- COUNT, local EXDATE, UTC EXDATE and a moved RECURRENCE-ID instance.
- Last Wednesday of the month, December BYMONTH and evaluation-window bounds.
- All-day dates in a positive fractional-offset display timezone across New Year.
- Unknown Exchange-style TZID with a fixed offset and embedded definitions
  taking precedence over recognized IANA names.
- Exchange-style recurring observances, for meetings away from the transition.
- A directly constructed custom timezone: exact UTC transition boundaries and
  local gaps/folds, including the ordering of ambiguous instants.

CI reruns all three groups in separate processes under UTC, Europe/Berlin,
America/New_York and Asia/Kolkata. Tests do not change process-global TZ.
`cargo test --locked` retains the committed dependency and bundled chrono-tz
data versions. Review changes to expected instants when updating those versions.

## Fixed timezone regressions

These regressions run normally in CI:

| Test | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `negative_fractional_offset` | `-0330` is minus 3 hours 30 minutes, so 09:00 local is 12:30 UTC |
| `exchange_transition_instant` | Onsets use TZOFFSETFROM; exact spring and autumn boundaries resolve correctly |

The transition fixture tests the parsed zone directly to isolate construction
from event recurrence. Timezone unit tests also cover signed minutes/seconds,
invalid offsets, non-recurring observances, and inclusive UTC UNTIL bounds with
positive and negative pre-transition offsets. Construction uses local onset
fields minus TZOFFSETFROM, independently of the viewer and host timezones.

## Additional edge-case contracts

- Missing local times use the pre-transition offset; repeated times choose the
  first instant. This applies to explicit datetimes and generated recurrences,
  following RFC 5545 section 3.3.5 and verified erratum 4271:
  https://www.rfc-editor.org/errata/eid4271
- IANA and custom European gaps/folds and a 30-minute Lord Howe gap are covered.
- Any nonzero number of observances is supported; an empty zone returns an error.
  A three-observance history verifies that ended DST rules stay ended.
- Observance RDATE lists and repeated RDATE properties supply transitions across
  multiple years. DTSTART and the last pre-window onset are retained as needed.
- All EXDATE properties and comma-separated values are resolved in their own
  timezone and matched by instant, after recurrence expansion. Tests distinguish
  the two instants in a fold, and exclude every occurrence without resurrecting
  the master event.

## Remaining migration coverage

This is an initial suite, not full RFC conformance or approval to replace the
fork. Extend it with anonymized real Exchange calendars and contracts for:

- Event-level RDATE (distinct from observance RDATE).
- Floating recurrences and all-day durations across DST.
- End-to-end southern hemisphere recurrences and date-line changes.
- Broader malformed-input coverage and bounded expansion of unending rules.

For a candidate library, run the same contracts and investigate every difference.
Keep intended behavior fixes distinct from regressions; the fork is a comparison
baseline, not an oracle.
